div.p: Reference guide for dispatchers, managers and drivers. Covers booking, planning, live tracking, the driver app, calling, AI document extraction and reporting.
There are three ways to create a Dispatch Booking (a prema.dispatch.job record, numbered DISP/YYYY/#####):
div.h3: From a Sales Order or Invoice
div.p: Click Book Load on the Sales Order or Invoice. If a booking already exists for that document, you'll be asked whether to open the existing one or create a separate one — this avoids duplicate bookings if the button is clicked twice.

On a Sales Order's Generate from Text tab, paste a customer WhatsApp message, SMS or email into the text box and click Generate Dispatch Booking. AI extracts the pickup/delivery stops, pallet counts per stop, route, date, and reefer/liftgate requirements, then creates the booking with stops already filled in — you just review and confirm.
Create a Dispatch Booking directly from the Dispatch Planner or backend list, filling in customer, reference/BOL/PO, stops, equipment and skid counts by hand.

Every booking moves through stages: Draft → New Booking → Planning → Assigned → Ready to Dispatch (booking phase), then Sent to Driver → En Route Pickup → At Pickup → Picked Up → In Transit → At Delivery → Delivered → POD Received (dispatched phase), ending at Completed, Exception or Cancelled.

ul.li: Booking Templates (Settings menu) — save a recurring lane's stop pattern to reuse for repeat customers.
Find Available Truck — mid-day load finder for slotting an ad-hoc booking onto a truck that already has room on its route.
LTL Consolidations (Reports menu) — combine multiple LTL bookings that share a lane onto one truck.

div.p: The Planner is the main scheduling board: unassigned jobs on one side, trucks with their assigned stops on the other.
div.h3: Assigning a Job to a Truck

ul.li: Drag and drop — drag a job card from the Unassigned panel onto a truck row.
Click to assign — click Assign on a job card, then click the target truck row.
If the system flags the assignment as infeasible (e.g. truck can't make the time window), a manager can confirm an override to force the assignment anyway.

tr.td: Requests Google-estimated arrival times for every stop on that truck's route.
Re-orders the truck's pending stops for the shortest total drive time.
Generates/refreshes that truck's Driver Worksheet for the day (stop count, total drive time, total detention time).

ul.li: Stop View / Block View — toggle the timeline between individual stop markers and stretched job blocks.

Layout modes: Normal / Wide / Multi — Wide collapses the side panels for more room; Multi (and the New Window button) opens a synced second Planner window for a two-monitor dispatch desk. Your choice is remembered between sessions.
Auto Plan — automatically assigns unassigned loads to the best-fit truck.
Feasibility — opens the feasibility checker for a job before assigning it.

div.p: The bottom map shows truck GPS and route with satellite/hybrid toggle and No Tolls / No Highways / No Ferries routing checkboxes. The Stops panel lets you drag-reorder stops on a truck, adjust service time with the +/- stepper, delete a stop, and see a pallet-capacity bar for the truck.
div.div: Hover over driver names, reefer/liftgate badges, the GPS-age indicator, or the ETAs/Optimize/Sheet buttons for a short delay to see a detail tooltip.

div.p: The Live Map menu shows every active truck's real-time GPS position alongside its remaining stops, refreshed automatically as drivers update their status in the Driver App. Use it to see at a glance where every truck is right now without opening individual bookings.

Customers get a scaled-down, privacy-filtered version of this: the public tracking page at /dispatch/track/<tracking number> shows their own stop's live ETA and status, with other stops on the truck shown only by city, and polls for updates every 30 seconds.
The Booking Board (managers only) is an airport-terminal-style status overview of every booking — a live table, not a kanban — refreshing every 20 seconds.
Booking #, Customer, Status, Pickup, Deadline, Route, Skids, Equipment, Priority, Truck, Driver, Feasibility, Notes.
Planned, Picked Up, In-Progress, Late, Delivered, Cancelled.

A strip above the table lists every booking with no truck yet — reference, feasibility badge, customer, route, pickup, skids, equipment, priority and notes — so nothing falls through the cracks before end of day.
Click the × button on any row to pull that booking back off its truck and return it to the Unassigned panel — the same action available from the Planner.
Drivers use the mobile web app at /dispatch/driver (add it to your phone's home screen for a full-screen app feel). Sign in with your driver account.

The Home screen shows a weekly calendar and today's summary; the Stops tab lists every stop in a flat list. Tap the map icon (⛶) for a fullscreen route map, or the gear (⚙) to set route options (avoid tolls / highways / ferries).

ul.li: Tap a stop to open its detail screen with a map and address.
Tap ✓ I'm Here in navigation once arrived — a geofence banner also prompts "You've arrived!" automatically within 150m of the stop.
Drag the pin in the pin editor and tap Save Pin to mark the exact parking/entrance spot, use 📡 My GPS for your current location, or 📍 Use Address to reset to the geocoded address.
Reorder stops, or adjust service time, from the stop list.
Tap ⚠ Report Issue to flag Road Closure, Business Closed, Recipient Unavailable, Address Not Found, or another problem — dispatch is notified immediately.

div.p: Attach entrance photos and delivery/POD photos per stop directly from the app; use the built-in document scanner (frame the page, capture, retake or enhance, then ✓ Use This) to photograph BOLs and paperwork with auto-cropping. A custody/POD photo is required before a transfer stop can be marked complete.

In-app turn-by-turn navigation with North-up/Heading-up toggle, voice guidance, fullscreen mode, a live distance badge, and a one-tap 🗺️ Open in Maps app handoff to Google/Apple Maps for full voice-guided driving directions.
Tap the 💬 icon to open an in-app chat thread with dispatch (unread messages show a badge on the icon); tap 📞 to call dispatch directly from any screen.
Dispatchers place and receive calls through Odoo's standard VoIP widget (top bar) — Prema Dispatch does not replace this, it adds two things on top of it:

ul.li: Team-wide call visibility — Dispatchers and Dispatch Managers can see every call in the call log, not just their own, so anyone can follow up on a customer or driver call.
Recording playback — calls that were recorded by the phone system show a Recording column with a ▶ play button in the call list; it streams the matched Asterisk recording for that call.

div.p: Instead of retyping a rate confirmation or route sheet by hand, upload it (or paste its text) and let AI read it:

ol.li: Open the AI Job Planner wizard (from an invoice's Add Dispatch Job action) and attach the rate confirmation / BOL / route sheet file(s), or paste the text directly.
Click Analyze with AI. The engine classifies the document (rate confirmation vs. stop sheet) and extracts stop addresses, company names, time windows, PO numbers, pallet counts and weights.
Review the Rate Confirmation Fields tab — extracted rate amount, BOL #, PO # and load reference — and the editable stops list, correcting anything the AI got wrong.
Click Create Job & Schedule, then use Book Load on the invoice to turn it into an active Dispatch Booking.

div.p: The same underlying AI is used for the Sales Order Generate from Text flow described in Booking a Load — every extraction also feeds a learning loop that improves future parsing accuracy.
All reports live under the Reports menu.

tr.td: All Jobs
Every booking, any stage, for browsing/searching.
Completed
Bookings that have finished, for closing out and billing checks.
Stops
Stop-by-stop detail for a driver/truck/date range, with total drive and detention time.
Driver Sheets
Historical Driver Worksheets (the live version also appears as its own top-level "Driver Worksheets" menu).
Freight Items
Line-item freight detail across bookings.
LTL Consolidations
Which bookings were combined onto shared LTL loads.
On-Time %
What percentage of completed stops arrived within their scheduled window, and average lateness.
Stop Time by Location
Which pickup/delivery locations have the longest average and worst-case dwell time.
Driver / Truck Performance
Jobs, stops, on-time %, and drive/detention time, grouped by driver or by truck.
Lane Profitability
Revenue, estimated cost and margin by origin → destination lane (managers only).
Fuel Efficiency
Which trucks are getting the worst km/L, from GeoTab-synced fuel telemetry.
Missed / Late Stops
Every late-arriving stop in a date range, worst lateness first.
POD Aging
Completed stops still missing proof-of-delivery evidence, oldest first.

div.p: A Load Plan is the physical record of one truck's actual loading for one day — which pallets go where inside the truck. It is separate from the financial booking(s) riding on that truck: one Load Plan can carry pallets from several different customers' bookings at once, but each booking's invoice, sales order, and revenue stay completely independent. Sharing a truck never merges two customers' accounting.

A physical pallet (prema.dispatch.item with load_unit_type pallet/shared pallet/container) occupies exactly one truck position. If that same pallet contains freight for more than one delivery stop (a shared skid), each stop it serves is a separate allocation record — the pallet count never multiplies by the number of stops. A pallet feeding 3 stops still counts as 1 pallet, 1 position, 3 allocations.

ul.li: Straight — the default for up to the template's straight capacity (12 for the seeded 26ft template). Lengthwise positions, driver side (L1-L6) and passenger side (R1-R6).

Pin-Wheel — automatically proposed (never silently applied) when confirmed pallets exceed Straight's capacity, e.g. a 13th pallet. Existing assignments are preserved wherever the position code still exists in the new template; anything that no longer fits becomes Unassigned.
Turned — higher-density angled positions requiring four-way-entry pallets and forklift access at both ends. Not a legal safety guarantee — a planning aid only.

p.i: All seeded 26ft templates ship as "unverified" until real interior measurements are entered on the template (Settings > Vehicle Layout Templates) — don't treat an unverified template's capacity as guaranteed. While unverified, the Planner shows an "UNVERIFIED VEHICLE LAYOUT" banner and a Dispatch Manager/Dispatcher must explicitly acknowledge it before Confirm Loading is allowed — this acknowledgement is logged in the Load Plan's event timeline. Turned is never auto-proposed while unverified; only Straight/Pin-Wheel are considered by the automatic capacity check.

div.p: Airline-seat-style tap interaction, both in the Dispatch Planner's Pallet Layout panel and the Driver App's Load Plan screen: tap a vacant (green) position, then pick an unassigned pallet to assign it there. Tap an occupied position to see its detail and Move/Swap/Unassign/Mark Loaded/Report Exception. No drag-and-drop is required on mobile.

Any material change after planning starts — a stop added/removed, a pallet's weight/dimensions changed, a job added to the truck — marks the plan stale. Existing pallet positions are never silently moved; the plan shows a stale banner until a dispatcher reviews it (Validate) and clears the flag.

A Load Plan locks automatically once the truck's job reaches the Picked Up stage (assuming validation passes — if not, the lock is deferred and flagged for dispatcher follow-up rather than blocking the actual pickup). Once locked, no one can rearrange pallets. A frozen snapshot of the entire plan (positions, pallets, stops, counts) is saved at that moment for claims/disputes. A Dispatch Manager can unlock with a mandatory reason, which is logged.

When a pallet moves to a different truck mid-route (the existing Driver Transfer feature), its Load Plan history follows it: the giving truck's Load Plan keeps a record of the handoff, the receiving truck's Load Plan gets the pallet as unassigned (never a blind copy of the old position — the new truck may use a different layout). The pallet's identity and financial job never change.

A "LOAD PLAN" status card on the driver's Stops screen shows loaded/unassigned/warning counts at a glance and opens the full diagram. Drivers can assign, move, mark loaded, report an exception, and confirm loading — all through the same tap interaction as the dispatcher panel. Locked plans block further edits.

Warehouse Loader accounts (a separate, more restricted role from Driver) sign in at /dispatch/warehouse to view active Load Plans, mark pallets loaded, move a pallet if permitted, and report damage — with no access to rates, invoices, or truck/driver reassignment. Every physical pallet also has a QR code; scanning it with a phone's normal camera opens a read-only summary (reference, truck, position, stop numbers, shared/exception status) with no financial data, and prompts for login before any write action.

Recommend Layout proposes positions using simple rules — earliest deliveries nearest the rear door, later deliveries farther forward, basic weight/side-balance and four-way-entry checks. It is always advisory: a dispatcher or driver must explicitly Accept or Reject before anything changes, and both the recommendation and the decision are logged.

Every Load Plan action goes through the same driver-ownership and record-state checks as the rest of the Driver App (Phase 1A). Drivers see only their own truck's plan; Warehouse Loaders see any operationally active plan but never financial data; only Dispatch Manager can unlock a locked plan.

ul.li: "No layout template available for this vehicle" — no layout template exists yet; add one under Settings > Vehicle Layout Templates, or leave a template's Applicable Vehicles blank to apply it generically.
"This load plan was updated by someone else" — another user (or the driver) saved a change first; refresh and retry your action.
Plan won't lock — check Validate for the specific blocking reason (usually an unassigned required pallet or capacity exceeded).
